name: Magnesium sulfate
status: PILOT – † lines checked against package insert 2026-11-15; awaiting review

pi_source.title: Adco Magnesium Sulphate 50% injection – professional information (SAHPRA repository, 21 Nov 2025)

dagger_note: † = general pharmacology; not in the SA guideline and not stated in the package insert consulted
item_format: t=text, s=source:printed page (s=pi: package insert), d=dagger, n=from own notes, b=bold, h=heading
summary: First-line anticonvulsant in eclampsia and severe pre-eclampsia; also used in acute severe asthma, torsades de pointes and hypomagnesaemia.

forms.t: Injection 50%: 2 mL ampoule = 1 g = 4 mmol magnesium

moa.t: Magnesium is a co-factor for many enzymes and is involved in neurochemical transmission and muscle excitability
Physiological calcium antagonist: reduces acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction and relaxes smooth muscle (bronchodilation)
NMDA-receptor antagonism and cerebral vasodilation are the proposed anticonvulsant mechanisms in eclampsia

pk.t: IV onset immediate, effect about 30 min; IM onset about 1 h, effect 3–4 h
Excreted by the kidney; impaired renal function can produce toxic blood levels

dosing.h: Eclampsia / severe pre-eclampsia – no infusion pump

items.t: Loading: 4 g IV in 200 mL sodium chloride 0.9% over 20 minutes
Then 5 g IM every 4 hours at different sites, until 24 h after delivery or after the last convulsion
PHC before referral: 4 g IV loading AND 10 g IM (5 g in each buttock), then 5 g IM every 4 hours in alternate buttocks
Loading: 4 g IV in 200 mL sodium chloride 0.9% over 20 minutes
Maintenance: 1 g every hour IV infusion, until 24 h after delivery or after the last convulsion

dosing.h: Recurrent eclamptic seizure after loading dose

items.t: 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) IV in 100 mL sodium chloride 0.9% over 20 minutes, single dose
2 g IV over 5–10 minutes; if episodes recur, 2 g IV over 24 hours
25–50 mg/kg IV over a few minutes

administration.t: IV: give as a 10% or 20% solution at a rate not exceeding 150 mg per minute; monitor blood pressure during each injection
IM doses are given at different sites

adjustments.t: Stop if urine output < 100 mL / 4 hours
Urine output should not fall below 25 mL/hour; toxicity develops at lower doses in renal failure
Crosses the placenta; monitor fetal heart rate; high doses can cause neonatal hypotonia and respiratory depression
Continuous use for more than 5–7 days can cause fetal skeletal adverse effects

contraindications.t: Heart block (class I–III), myocardial damage, myasthenia gravis
Renal failure, anuria, severe renal impairment
Hepatic encephalopathy or hepatic failure; intracranial pathology

cautions.t: Potentiates and prolongs non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers; additive neuromuscular block with aminoglycosides
Additive depression with barbiturates, opioids, hypnotics and anaesthetics – adjust their dose

adverse_effects.t: Flushing, nausea and vomiting, lethargy, drowsiness, thirst, muscle weakness
Hypotension, bradycardia, arrhythmias, prolonged PR / QRS / QT
Toxicity by serum level: reflexes diminished 2.1–2.9 mmol/L; reflexes lost, somnolence, hypotension 2.9–5 mmol/L; respiratory paralysis and cardiac arrest above 5 mmol/L

monitoring.t: STOP if knee reflexes absent, urine output < 100 mL / 4 hours, or respiratory rate < 16 / minute
Loss of the deep tendon reflex is the early clinical sign of intoxication

toxicity.t: Respiratory depression: calcium gluconate 10%, 10 mL IV slowly, not faster than 5 mL/minute
Keep injectable calcium gluconate immediately available; dialysis rapidly lowers magnesium in severe renal dysfunction

conflicts.t: Package insert advises avoiding use within 2 hours of delivery; the STG continues magnesium until 24 hours after delivery in eclampsia. The pathway follows the STG.
Package insert lists impaired renal function as a contraindication; the STG uses the urine-output stopping rule instead.
